name: matchingPairs.exists_linear_factor
summary: Define T(Ψ) as Λ of the function x ↦ χ(det k_x)·localSection(χ, firstCols(e, k_x))(Ψ) on primitive x (k_x ∈ GL_n(O) with x = invLastRows(e, k_x)); for a matched pair, cover the support of Φ by finitely many translates of the primitive set and use the invariance of Λ.

steps.claim: For every x whose transpose is primitive choose k(x) ∈ GL_n(O) with x = invLastRows(e, k(x)) (`exists_invLastRows_iff_transpose`, `IsValuationPair.exists_firstCols_iff`; K).
steps.lean:
choose! k _ K using
    (exists_invLastRows_iff_transpose e (x := ·).2 ∘ ((@valPair F _).exists_firstCols_iff _).2)

steps.claim: Take T = Λ ∘ (Ψ ↦ (x ↦ [xᵀ primitive]·χ(det k(x))·localSection(χ, firstCols(e, k(x)))(Ψ))).
steps.lean:
use Λ ∘ₗ .pi fun x ↦
    ite (IsPrimitiveMatrix O xᵀ) (χ (k x).det) 0 • localSection χ (firstCols e (k x))

steps.claim: Let (Φ, Ψ) be a matched pair: Φ is Schwartz–Bruhat with support in the surjective matrices (m) and h is the matching identity.

Choose representatives r_q of GL_a(F)/GL_a(O) with the properties of `exists_common_coset_reps` (S: finite sums; R: for every left-invertible y, exactly one q with y·r_q primitive and exactly one q with y·r_q⁻¹ primitive, the representatives serving both directions).
steps.lean: choose r S R using (@exists_common_coset_reps F _ a n).choose_spec

steps.claim: For every coset q, the function x ↦ Φ(x)·[xᵀ·r_q⁻¹ primitive] (Φ cut down to the preimage of the primitive set under x ↦ xᵀ·r_q⁻¹; Lean's `(r q).2` is the inverse of r_q) is Schwartz–Bruhat: an indicator of a clopen set (`TameLocalChar.isClopen_primitive`) times Φ.
steps.lean:
have o q : _ ∈ schwartzBruhat _ :=
    ⟨(LocallyConstant.indicator ⟨_, m.1⟩ ((hχ.isClopen_primitive _ e).preimage
    (f := (·ᵀ * (r q).2)) (by fun_prop))).2, m.2.imp (·.mono (by simp)) (.trans (by simp))⟩

steps.claim: For every x in the support of Φ choose its coset p(x), the unique q with xᵀ·r_q⁻¹ primitive (U: the uniqueness in that direction).
The support of Φ is compact (its closure is), so finitely many of these open translates cover it: a finite set t of cosets.
steps.lean:
let ⟨t, ht⟩ := ((m.1 {0}).isClosed_compl.closure_eq.subst m.2.1).elim_finite_subcover _
    (o · |>.1 {0}ᶜ) fun _ ↦ by simp; tauto

steps.claim: Λ(Φ) = ∑_{q∈t} Λ(cut-down of Φ at q), and by the invariance hΛ applied to transposeGL(r_q) each term is Λ of the function x ↦ χ(det r_q)·(cut-down at q)(r_qᵀ·x), whose indicator [(r_qᵀx)ᵀ·r_q⁻¹ primitive] = [xᵀ primitive] (the weighted change of variables is by r_qᵀ); it remains to compare the summed functions pointwise in x.
steps.lean:
convert congr(∑ q ∈ t, $(hΛ (transposeGL (r q)) _ (o q))) <;> simp only [← map_smul, ← map_sum,
    Λ.comp_apply] <;> congr with x <;> simp [-ite_smul, Set.indicator, Set.subset_def] at ht U ⊢

steps.claim: Split on whether xᵀ is primitive.
If xᵀ is primitive: by the matching identity h at k(x) and the finite-sum property S, the value is χ(det k(x))·localSection(χ, firstCols(e, k(x)))(Ψ) (K).
steps.lean: apply (sub_eq_zero.1 congr($h _) ▸ S t ..).trans <;> simp [← K _ ‹_›]

steps.claim: The remaining pointwise identities: only the term q = p(x) of the sum over t survives (`Finset.sum_eq_single`, by the uniqueness U), and outside the primitive set both sides vanish.
steps.lean: repeat grind [t.sum_eq_single (p x), fun q _ ↦ (U ((r q).1ᵀ * x) · q (by simpa))]
